items.answer:
**FY2026 Q3**

Meta launched Muse, a personal agent designed to enhance user productivity and engagement, during this quarter. The launch was described as one of their most successful, with over 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada setting up Muse personal agents within the first six weeks. Engagement and retention rates have been strong, with about 25% of users engaging with Muse daily, which is noted to be more than twice the level of engagement seen with Threads at its launch [4][9].

The most common use cases for Muse include shopping, personal productivity, and creativity, with over 25% of weekly active users engaging in shopping activities. The average purchase size for shopping through Muse exceeds $200 [4][2]. Meta's strategy involves scaling Muse to serve billions of users, leveraging its existing Family of Apps user base, which currently stands at 3.64 billion daily users [4][1].

In terms of monetization, Meta plans to offer Muse for free to most users while generating revenue through commerce tools and subscriptions for advanced features. They anticipate that Muse will reach higher average revenue levels compared to existing Family of Apps users, which currently averages several hundreds of dollars annually [1][2].
